words.sense: A strong and recurring liking for a particular activity or thing.
misconceptions: Assumes a preference is an uncontrollable tendency.

words.sense: A recurring disposition or tendency to behave in a certain way, whether liked or not.
misconceptions: Assumes a preference is an uncontrollable tendency.

semantic_axes.description: A penchant is something a person likes doing; a propensity is something a person tends to do, with or without liking it.

edges.boundary_rule: A penchant is something a person likes doing; a propensity is something a person tends to do, with or without liking it.

misconceptions.M2: Assumes a preference is an uncontrollable tendency.
misconceptions.M3: Ignores whether the subject wants the repeated behaviour.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Rina’s habit of trying unusual drinks?

beats.text: Rina looks for unfamiliar drinks on every menu and smiles when she finds one to order.
beats.decisive_clue: deliberately seeks unfamiliar drinks she enjoys
beats.reason: The first beat supplies the deciding evidence: deliberately seeks unfamiliar drinks she enjoys.

beats.text: She keeps a list of favourites to try again.
beats.decisive_clue: deliberately seeks unfamiliar drinks she enjoys
beats.reason: Choosing and repeating an activity for pleasure points to a liking.

chains.feedback_short: Deliberately seeks unfamiliar drinks she enjoys is what distinguishes penchant here.
chains.feedback_deep: Penchant means a strong and recurring liking for a particular activity or thing. Propensity means a recurring disposition or tendency to behave in a certain way, whether liked or not. Here, deliberately seeks unfamiliar drinks she enjoys; choosing and repeating an activity for pleasure points to a liking.
